blocks.text: A more difficult question is why, in Matth. XII, 24. and Luc. XI, 15., the Pharisees held that Beel-zebub, or Beel-zebul, was the prince of demons, whom other Hebrews call אשמודי, Asmodaeus. I have no answer to give, except that the Philistine city Accaron [Ekron] is also written Acharon by Jerome and others. Since this closely echoes Acheron, the god of Acharon could have been confused by the ignorant with the god of [III, 352] Acheron, that is, with Pluto, whom the theology of the gentiles set over the underworld. For it is well known that the later Hebrews derived not a few words of their own language from the Greek. An example is that Josephus holds that τὰ Ἱεροσόλυμα [ta Hierosolyma] is so called because of τὸ ἱερὸν [to hieron], that is, the temple built there. And the same author calls the torrent Iabok Iobacchus, as though it were named after the god Iobacchus. The same was the intention of those who first said, for the torrents Kedron and Kison, χειμάῤῥους τῶν κέδρων [cheimarrhous tōn kedrōn] and τῶν κισσῶν [tōn kissōn], as if they were so called from cedars and pitch-pines. And the city Scitta was called Scythopolis, as though from the Scythians. And AR of the Moabites became Ἀρεόπολις [Areopolis], as if the city of Mars. And the name Taphnes was changed into Daphnes, so that it might be believed to be called παρὰ τῶν ἐκεῖ πολλῶν φυομένων δαφνῶν [para tōn ekei pollōn phyomenōn daphnōn], from the many laurels planted there. Finally, for the same reason, from the Philistines were made Ἀλλόφυλοι [Allophyloi], from Pibeseth Βούβαστος [Boubastos], from the Giblites the Byblians, from the Horites the City of Heroes, from Iabneel Ἰάμνια [Iamnia], as if it had this name ὅτι Ἰάμνους ἐκάλουν τοὺς καθύγρους, καὶ τεθηλότας τόπους [hoti Iamnous ekaloun tous kathygrous, kai tethēlotas topous], because they called moist and verdant places ἰάμνους [iamnous]. So Stephanus. And Ptolemais, for עכו Accho, was called Ἄκη [Akē], as though from τοῦ ἀκεῖν [tou akein], because Hercules was healed there.
